rationale: C02 plausibly supplied a material template for the short child letter. Both endorse a private civic campaign framed as part of the international struggle for freedom, then appeal for Americans to join the recipient's effort. The especially close construction—“I hope that all citizens will join with you” versus “I hope that all Americans will join with you”—is concrete shared language central to each letter, not merely routine correspondence boilerplate. C16 has a similar endorsement-and-mobilization structure, while C24 shares the telegram-response form but not the child's substantive drafting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your telegram of April twenty-sixth ... meets with my heartiest approval.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is for these reasons that I am happy to accept the Honorary Chairmanship of Brotherhood Week 1950.
shared_material.explanation: Each letter formally endorses participation in a private national civic campaign after framing its larger moral significance.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hope that all Americans will join with you in dedicating themselves to this critical struggle for men's minds.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hope that all citizens will join with you as General Chairman and with the National Conference of Christians and Jews to help make justice, amity and understanding the daily practice of our nation.
shared_material.explanation: This is a close and distinctive syntactic match: a presidential hope that all Americans/citizens will “join with you” in advancing the recipient's organized campaign.

shared_material.child_excerpt: this critical struggle for men's minds
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Respect for human dignity is the central issue in the world struggle today ... stand united ... for the achievement of that peace and freedom
shared_material.explanation: Both situate the requested civic participation within the contemporary ideological struggle for freedom and human dignity.
